# DropSpace 1.1 Beta4

<!-- update-summary: Adds configurable low-latency liquid glass, four refresh tiers and adjustable expanded refraction width. Includes a Music window widget, optional island hiding while that window is visible, interface-aware translation defaults and improved alignment. -->

## Changes

- The existing island gains an independently implemented GPU liquid-glass material. Background blur, edge refraction, RGB dispersion and a black-to-glass gradient affect only the material behind the original content.
- Settings include island material, background blur (0–30), refraction (0–400%), expanded refraction width (50–300%), dispersion (0–100), dark overlay (0–200%) and Ink glass, the gradient switch, in all ten UI languages. Width **100%** restores the initial edge band; **200%** doubles its expanded influence while leaving the compact material unchanged.
- The requested defaults are liquid glass, blur **1**, refraction **100%**, expanded width **200%**, dispersion **75**, dark overlay **0%**, and Ink glass **on**. Resident display and the idle logo default to **off**. Existing saved preferences are preserved.
- Four glass refresh tiers are available: Standard (30 fps), High (60 fps), Very high (120 fps), and Ultra (the island monitor's current refresh rate). Standard remains the default. Latest-frame replacement and direct island-region processing reduce stale-frame delay and unnecessary copies without lowering sampling quality. Actual delivery depends on Windows, the display and GPU workload.
- Acrylic remains selectable and hides the glass controls while retaining their values. Liquid Glass exposes only Liquid Glass material in the appearance selector; switching back restores the saved Acrylic appearance. Unavailable capture or graphics support falls back to the previous material. High contrast, reduced effects, disabled transparency and remote sessions retain their existing accessible fallback behavior.

- The optional **Music window** widget opens or restores the single independent music window. Existing widget arrangements are preserved. The widget, music-page button, window title and related setting use a consistent name.
- A new opt-in setting hides automatic island presentations while the Music window is visible, even with resident display enabled. Minimizing or closing that window restores the current presence rules. Explicit retrieval, file dragging and position adjustment remain available; ending those temporary interactions resumes hiding.
- Before a manual translation-language choice, Chinese interfaces default to Chinese and other interfaces to English. Explicit choices and existing saved targets remain independent of later interface changes. Lyrics providers, matching, models and translation processing are unchanged.
- Settings controls align vertically with their labels, and the main music page's empty-state message is centered.

The existing island content, geometry, typography, toolbar, controls and hit targets are preserved. The live glass material uses in-memory desktop sampling and excludes the island from screenshots and recordings to prevent self-feedback. No screen image is stored or transmitted by this material.

v1.1.0-beta.3 is the immediate upgrade baseline for this release. Existing settings, content, lyrics matching, source preferences, model files and independent CUDA component bytes are preserved.

## Compatibility and verification

Windows x64 build 20348 or later. See the [material validation record](../../docs/dev/1.1-beta4-liquid-glass.md), [refresh measurements](../../docs/dev/1.1-beta4-glass-refresh-tiers.md) and [music-window validation record](../../docs/dev/1.1-beta4-music-window.md) for actual checks and limits.

The pre-existing native heap crash (`0xc0000374`) has not been proven fixed. This update does not claim long-term native stability, or validation across every GPU, monitor/DPI combination or remote-session configuration.
